heard: Can you measure the whole earth with a stick? You don't walk around it, and you don't need space. You need noon. Find a town where the noon sun shines straight down a well. In Sayin, on the longest day, there's no shadow at all. Same day, same noon, stand to stick up in Alexandria, far to the north. It casts a shadow 7 .2 degrees. Sunlight arrives in parallel lines. So that angle is also the slice of earth between the two towns. And 7 .2 degrees is 1 .50th of a circle. The whole earth is just 50 of those slices. Pay a surveyor to pace the distance, 5 ,000 stadia. Times 50 is 250 ,000. Historians still argue how long a stadium was. The short one gives 40 ,000 kilometers. The real answer, 40 ,000 eight. Try it yourself. With a friend 1 ,000 kilometers south, your noon shadows differ by about 9 degrees. So if your friend's 500 kilometers away, how far apart are your shadows?
